conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have two children I'm asking about - Alex who's 16 and Blake who's 11. They both live with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have two children - Alex (16) and Blake (11) - who both live with you in the UK.

Since Alex is 16, I need to understand their situation a bit more, as the rules differ for children aged 16 and over. Let me ask:

**Is Alex still in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I'm not entirely sure about that right now. Alex has just turned 16 recently and we're still figuring out what they're doing next - whether they'll continue with college or look at other options. I don't have those details sorted yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. It's understandable that things are still being decided since Alex has just turned 16.

Let me ask you a few more questions about your general circumstances:

**Are you responsible for both Alex and Blake?** By this I mean, do you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation, or contribute at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after both of them - I provide all their food, clothes, put a roof over their heads, everything they need really. They're my kids and I take care of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming. Now I need to understand a bit about your residency status to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here?** (For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, or another immigration status?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based here in Manchester actually, and yes, I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Are either Alex or Blake currently:**
- In hospital or residential care for an extended period?
- Living with someone else?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Claiming benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that applies. They both live at home with me full-time. Neither of them are in hospital or any kind of care, and they're not working - they're just kids really. Blake's only 11, so definitely not working or claiming anything. And Alex isn't working or claiming any benefits either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just clarify one final point:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake?** (For example, another parent or guardian)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them. It's just me looking after them both.

## Summary

**For Blake (age 11): ELIGIBLE** ✓
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake. They are under 16, live with you in the UK, you're responsible for them, and all the eligibility criteria are met.

**For Alex (age 16): INDETERMINATE** ⚠️
I cannot determine eligibility for Alex at this time because they are 16 years old. For children aged 16-19, they must be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit. Since Alex has just turned 16 and you're still figuring out whether they'll go to college or pursue other options, I don't have enough information to assess their eligibility.

## What this means

- You can definitely claim Child Benefit for Blake
- Once you know whether Alex will be continuing in approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, or certain training programs), you'll be able to determine if you can continue claiming for them too
- If Alex does continue in approved education or training, you would likely remain eligible for Child Benefit for them until they turn 20 (or leave education/training)

If you find out Alex's plans and would like me to reassess their eligibility, please let me know!
